article.Citation/Title: MacLean, J. R., MacDonald, D. C., Byrne, U. P., & Hubbard, A. M. (1961). The use of LSD-25 in the treatment of alcoholism and other psychiatric problems. Quarterly Journal of Studies on Alcohol, 22, 34-45.
article.SourcePDF: alcohol/MacLean, J. R., MacDonald, D. C., Byrne, U. P., & Hubbard, A. M. (196. The use of LSD-25 in the treatment of alcoholism and other psychiatric problems.pdf
article.InterventionDescription: Single oral dose of LSD-25 (400-1,500 gamma, titrated) in one-day hospital session with 4-person therapeutic group; symbolic setting, overnight stay, and post-session counselor support.

ae_events.Description: Transient nausea occurring roughly 1/2 to 2 hours after LSD-25 ingestion; described as a typical side effect.
Mild headache occurring roughly 1/2 to 2 hours after LSD-25 ingestion, per authors' own description.
Mild gastric distress occurring roughly 1/2 to 2 hours after LSD-25 ingestion, per authors' own description.
In-session anxiety/tension reported across multiple cases (e.g., 'moderate degree of tension,' 'increasing tension,' 'apprehension and oppression').
Perceptual distortions in the visual field, reported by one patient (Case 43) about 4 hours after LSD-25 ingestion.
Confused, disorganized speech and disorientation during the session (Case 29); no improvement in mental condition noted at discharge 6 days later.

article.Outcome: Primary and only reported outcome is the composite improvement rating (much improved / improved / unchanged) for the alcoholic subgroup, which for alcoholics is explicitly anchored to abstinence or reduced drinking versus the prior 12 months (Evaluation section; Table 1-A 'Totals' row). 30 much improved + 16 improved = 46/61 (75.4%) vs 15/61 (24.6%) unchanged. No other primary endpoint is designated anywhere in the article. Note: the 'Composite Totals' row at the foot of Table 1 (68 M / 34 F) is arithmetically inconsistent with the sum of the A and B subgroup totals (50+16=66 M), likely an OCR/print artifact in the source table; it was not used because the alcoholic-only subgroup total (61) is internally self-consistent (50 M + 11 F = 61; 30+16+15 = 61) and is the correct population for this Alcohol-condition extraction.
article.SD: No dispersion or test statistic is reported anywhere in the article for the improvement-rate outcome; results are purely descriptive counts with no significance testing performed. Coded '.'.
article.PVal: No p-value is reported for the treatment outcome anywhere in the article (Results, Summary, or Discussion). Coded '.'.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: 61 — the alcoholic subgroup (Table 1-A Totals: 50 M + 11 F = 61), not the full 100-patient series (61 alcoholics + 39 non-alcoholics with other psychiatric disabilities). Outcome is drawn from the alcoholic subgroup's own results table since Condition = Alcohol. All 61 are accounted for across the three outcome categories (30+16+15=61), so no further attrition adjustment was needed.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: Objective, design, setting, intervention, outcome criteria, results, and harms (Side Effects paragraph) are all described. Not described: formal a priori eligibility/exclusion criteria (sample characteristics are given post hoc instead), the absence of a comparator/control group is never explicitly acknowledged, sample size is given but no power rationale, randomization and blinding are never mentioned (not even as absent), no statistical methods/tests are described (purely descriptive counts), and no funding source or conflict-of-interest statement is given (only acknowledgment of clinical/AA staff assistance). n_met=7 < 13, so MethodologyDescribedYN=0.

article.RandomizationYN: Coded 0, not 3. Single-arm, open-label case series (100 patients, all received LSD-25; no control/comparison group). Per the single-arm boundary-case rule, the absent design element is coded 0.
article.BlindingYN: Coded 0, not 3, for the same single-arm/open-label reason.
article.Comparator: Coded 0, not 3. No control or comparison arm exists; all 100 patients received the same LSD-25 protocol.
article.Retention (%): Coded 100. Study is not randomized, so the denominator is the enrolled/treated alcoholic subgroup (61). All 61 are accounted for within the three outcome categories in Table 1-A (30+16+15=61), implying no attrition from the reported analysis. Not stated explicitly as a retention percentage by the authors — inferred from the completeness of Table 1-A.
article.ConfoundYN: Coded 1. Outcomes are stratified by diagnostic subgroup throughout (Table 1, Results, Discussion — e.g., differential response noted for 'sociopathic disturbance' vs 'personality trait disturbance' vs 'addiction with chronic brain damage'), substantively addressing diagnosis as a factor related to outcome, though no formal statistical adjustment for other covariates (age, sex, dose) is reported.
article.InclusionExclusionCriteria: Coded 0. The Sample section describes characteristics of the 61 selected alcoholics post hoc (delirium tremens history, prior AA failure, years of uncontrolled drinking) but never states a priori inclusion or exclusion criteria used to select the 61 from the 492 total admissions.
article.ValidatedScaleMeasYN: Coded 0. The Blewett Psychedelic Scales (A and B) assess the character of the psychedelic experience itself, not a validated clinical or substance-use outcome measure; the composite improvement rating (much improved/improved/unchanged) is an author-devised clinical rating, not a published/validated instrument.
article.PhysicalChangeMeasured: Coded 0. 'Clinical examination, including certain blood chemistry studies' was collected as pretreatment/baseline data (Collection of Data, section A.3), but the authors explicitly defer these findings 'to be discussed in another paper' and report no physical/biological change outcome within this article.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 0. The 61 alcoholics are a severity-selected subset (~12%) of 492 total hospital admissions for alcohol intoxication over 18 months, specifically chosen as 'difficult cases' (59/61 with prior delirium tremens, 36/61 having failed AA) rather than a representative cross-section of the admitted population.
article.PercentFem: 18.0 (11/61), computed from Table 1-A Totals row (50 M, 11 F) for the alcoholic subgroup, consistent with the SampleSize_NFinal denominator used for Outcome.
article.BaseStatus: Coded 'Severe'. Sample section reports an average of 14.36 years of uncontrolled drinking, average 8.07 hospital admissions for alcoholism in the preceding 3 years, 59/61 with prior delirium tremens, and 36/61 having failed Alcoholics Anonymous; authors state the group's prognosis 'would be unfavorable.'
article.Age_Median: Coded '.'. No aggregate mean or median age is reported for the alcoholic subgroup or the full 100-patient sample; only individual case-example ages (44-64) are given, which cannot be generalized to a sample-level bracket.
article.Followup in months: 18, the maximum of the reported range ('follow-up has been carried on for periods ranging from 3 to 18 months, the median being 9.09 months'). The protocol also describes a planned 1-year (12-month) interview, but 18 months is the longest duration explicitly reported as achieved in the Results.
article.AE_denominator: Coded 'Not numbered'. No explicit safety-population size is stated in the Side Effects paragraph; the implied denominator is the full treated series (N=100), but this figure is never restated numerically alongside the side-effect descriptions.
article.NParticipantsWithAE: Coded '.'. No aggregate count of patients experiencing at least one side effect is given; only a general 'typical side effects' statement and four illustrative case narratives are provided.

ae_events.MacLean 1961_AE01: Onset 'in-session': occurs 1/2-2 hours after 8:20 AM dosing, within the session day (session runs through the afternoon). Severity 'Mild' via rubric (transient, expected, no intervention described); authors gave no severity adjective for nausea specifically, unlike 'mild headache' and 'mild gastric distress'.
ae_events.MacLean 1961_AE03: SeveritySource='author': text explicitly states 'mild gastric distress.'
ae_events.MacLean 1961_AE04: Aggregates in-session anxiety/tension described in the general Procedure section and in multiple case examples (Case 43 'moderate degree of tension'; Case 2 explicitly labeled 'adverse effects in the form of increasing tension'; Case 5 'feelings of apprehension and oppression'). Graded 'Moderate' using Case 43's own author-assigned qualifier ('moderate') as the representative severity marker for this recurring AE type; per the rubric, expected in-session anxiety defaults to Mild absent intervention need or persistence, but the authors' own 'moderate' language for this type is treated as author-sourced grading. InterventionRequired coded '.' because the protocol's response to persistent anxiety ('more LSD-25 is needed') is a dosing decision, not a clearly-described rescue intervention.
ae_events.MacLean 1961_AE05: Perceptual distortions (Case 43, visual field, ~4 hours post-dose) graded 'Mild' via rubric — expected acute drug-effect phenomenology, no intervention or functional consequence described.
ae_events.MacLean 1961_AE06: SeverityIndeterminate='Y'. Case 29 shows confused, disorganized speech during the session and 'no improvement in her mental condition on the day of discharge, 6 days after' the session — persistence beyond the dosing day would indicate Moderate per the rubric's operational band definitions. However, this same patient was independently documented as disoriented, with poor memory and slurred/disconnected speech, 3-5 days BEFORE treatment (pre-existing cognitive impairment, plausibly alcohol-related). It cannot be determined from the text whether the persisting confusion at discharge reflects a drug-emergent AE or her unresolved pre-existing baseline state. Graded 'Moderate' on the persistence signal but flagged indeterminate due to this baseline confound; recommend human review. InterventionRequired coded '.' — no explicit intervention for her confusion is described.

config_proposal.note: Single-arm, uncontrolled case series with no comparator arm; only a pre/post composite improvement rate is available for the alcoholic subgroup (46/61 much improved or improved vs 15/61 unchanged, anchored to abstinence/reduced drinking for the alcoholics), which has no defensible conversion to a comparative Tier-1 effect size (d, g, eta_p, F, chi2, OR, or RR).
config_proposal.tier2_basis: 75.4% (46/61) of the alcoholic subgroup was rated much improved or improved on the composite outcome (which for alcoholics required abstinence or a definite reduction in drinking versus the prior 12 months), a directionally positive single-arm result with no control group.
